arml-2006-superrelay-01.prompt: Currently, Arnold is $3x$ years old and his younger sister Millie is $x$ years old. When Millie was born, Arnold was $16$ years old. Compute Arnold's age $10$ years from now.

arml-2006-superrelay-02.prompt: Let $T=34$. A right circular cylinder has a radius of $r$, a height of $Tr$, and a total surface area of $420\pi$. Compute $r$.

arml-2006-superrelay-05.prompt: Let $T=4$. A class has $T$ boys and $T$ girls and the heights of all the students are different. Compute the number of ways to arrange the students in a row such that all of the following conditions hold: (i) the boys are not all standing next to each other, (ii) from left to right the boys are arranged from shortest to tallest, and (iii) from left to right the girls are neither arranged from shortest to tallest, nor from tallest to shortest.

arml-2006-superrelay-06.prompt: Let $T=1430$. Let $K=\dfrac{2006-T}{4}$. The product of the positive divisors of $36^3$ equals $\left(2^{K+x}\right)\left(3^{K+y}\right)$ where $x$ and $y$ are integers. Compute $x+y$.

arml-2006-superrelay-07.prompt: Let $T=6$. Compute the maximum value of the function $f(x)=4\sin^2x+(T-2)\cos x+34$.

arml-2006-superrelay-08.prompt:
In the magic square below the sums of the elements in the rows, columns, and diagonals are all equal. Let $R=39$ and $T=42$.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 30&&\\\hline 27&&R\\\hline T&X&\\\hline\end{array}$$
Compute $X$.

arml-2006-superrelay-09.prompt: Let $T=4\sqrt3$. Triangle $ABC$ is given with $BC=2006$. Circle $O$ is inscribed in $\triangle ABC$, it is tangent to $\overline{AB}$ at $D$, and it has a radius of $1/T^2$. If $AD=10$, compute the area of $\triangle ABC$.

arml-2006-superrelay-10.prompt: Let $T=2$. A regular polygon of $T+1$ sides has a side length of $1$, an area of $K$, and a perimeter of $P$. Compute $P/K$.

arml-2006-superrelay-11.prompt: Let $T=14$. Two candles of height $T$ cm are lit. One burns down three times as fast as the other and after $T$ minutes, it is $1/5$ as tall as the other. Compute the height in centimeters of the fast burner after $T$ minutes.

arml-2006-superrelay-12.prompt: Let $T=6$. Arrange $T$ women and $T$ men into $T$ rows of $2$ people so that each row contains $1$ woman and $1$ man. Let $2^K$ be the highest power of $2$ that is a factor of the number of ways to do this. Compute $K$.

arml-2006-superrelay-14.prompt: Let $T=6$. In triangle $ABC$, $\angle ABC$ is a right angle, $AB=BC=12$, and $D$ is the midpoint of $\overline{BC}$. Point $E$ lies on $\overline{AB}$ with $BE=T$, and $F$ is the intersection of $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{CE}$. Compute $BF^2$.

arml-2006-superrelay-15.prompt: Let $a_1=1$, $a_2=11$, $a_3=111$, $a_4=1111$, and so on. Compute the smallest value of $n$ so that $a_n$ is a multiple of $n+1$.
